observation: Production serves config/analytics.json with enabled=true while the same file note says to keep it disabled until account and privacy approval; no Plausible, GA4, CRM, Resend delivery, or sales export was available to prove collection or outcomes.
evidence: Live config/analytics.json equals HEAD; assets/main.js; api/contact.js; repository search found no analytics/CRM delivery export
affected_scope: All organic landing and RFQ reporting
business_impact: The team cannot reliably connect search impressions or clicks to contact arrival, delivery, qualification, samples, quotes, or wins.
recommended_action: Verify the analytics account, domain, privacy position, and current event receipt before interpreting any conversion result.
dependencies: Plausible or GA4 access; owner decision on privacy and consent
acceptance_test: A dated test record proves page view and RFQ events reach the approved account without PII, or analytics is explicitly disabled and Privacy is aligned.
rollback: Set analytics enabled=false and remove only unverified event loading; preserve the form and email path.

observation: Implement a minimum auditable funnel with separate definitions for organic_landing, product_cta, contact_arrival, rfq_start, rfq_submit_client, rfq_delivered, qualified_rfq, sample_request, quote_sent, and won_project.
evidence: assets/main.js currently fires only RFQ Submit after HTTP 200; api/contact.js does not persist a provider delivery id or sales qualification
business_impact: Creates a decision-grade link from SEO entry to commercial outcome and prevents impressions from being used as a sales proxy.
recommended_action: Instrument approved non-PII events and a private operational record for provider acceptance and sales qualification; publish a 28-day scorecard.
dependencies: YSEO-001; event dictionary; CRM or controlled sheet; approved test recipient
acceptance_test: A controlled test traces one inquiry through every applicable stage and a 28-day export segments landing page, source, product, country, and outcome.
rollback: Disable new events and remove the new operational fields while retaining the current form delivery path.

observation: Production baseline b86702b contained unsupported operational percentages and broad regulatory statements: 90% cup bundle uptake, 80% single-line starts, 20% lead-time reduction, 3M+ shipments, 16 IP assets, blanket FDA/510(k)/CE recommendations, and ISO/cleanroom claims without public scope evidence.
evidence: Production releases e1613c9 and 1363466 revised 20 high-risk content pages, including the Pads/Liners material, 20% lead-time, format, and MOQ boundaries, and aligned the Chinese Home, Products, and Quality claims; docs/evidence/evidence-manifest.csv records pending source evidence. The live 30-URL claim scan passed; source approvals remain pending.
affected_scope: Home, About, Products, Quality, priority resource guides, and Chinese pages
business_impact: Unverifiable or overbroad statements can reduce buyer trust, create compliance risk, and make snippets or external distribution unsafe.
recommended_action: Create an approved claim register; remove or qualify any claim without entity, scope, source, jurisdiction, validity period, and public-use approval.
dependencies: Current certificates, test files, operational source data, and owner approval
acceptance_test: A claim scan and manual review find no unsupported percentage, certification, approval, registration, or market requirement; every retained high-risk claim maps to an approved record.
rollback: Restore the prior copy from a content backup only after Compliance approves the old wording.

observation: Rewrite regulatory guidance by product and intended use instead of presenting FDA registration, 510(k), or CE marking as universal requirements.
evidence: Current FDA and EU official guidance verified 2026-08-10; every identified production regulatory section now states intended-use and classification dependencies, explains that registration/listing is not FDA approval and CE marking applies only when specific EU legislation requires it, and uses official-source links. The live 30-URL wording scan passed; Compliance/legal review remains pending.
affected_scope: Regulatory sections and FAQs across Quality, product, and priority resource pages
business_impact: Accurate buyer guidance can become a trust advantage and avoids steering buyers toward the wrong document pack.
recommended_action: Replace blanket rules with a market-review workflow, link current official sources, state intended-use dependencies, and require Compliance review dates.
acceptance_test: Each affected page names product category, intended-use dependency, official source, review date, and owner; no page says FDA-approved based on registration or CE-required for all products.
rollback: Revert only the reviewed paragraph set; keep a dated copy of the prior wording for comparison.

observation: The Quality Evidence page is primarily a request path; public assets are a line sheet, RFQ checklist, and illustrative QC checklist, while approved redacted certificate scope, test summaries, and real QC release samples are absent.
evidence: /quality/evidence/; downloads/; docs/seo/authority-growth-weekly-2026-07-27.md
affected_scope: Quality, About, product pages, editorial distribution, and buyer due diligence
business_impact: Buyers and editors have little independent evidence to verify, cite, or use before submitting an RFQ.
recommended_action: Publish at least one approved, redacted, versioned evidence set with scope, issuer, entity, dates, limitations, and a clear illustrative/real label.
dependencies: Source files; redaction review; public-use approval
acceptance_test: The evidence page exposes approved files without personal/customer data; each file has scope, issue/expiry or review date, owner, and withdrawal process.
rollback: Unpublish the file and remove its card while preserving the evidence request path.

observation: Make /quality/evidence/ a mixed public-evidence and request-more hub, then connect it from Home, About, Quality, Products, Resources, and RFQ flows.
evidence: Production release e1613c9 publishes the mixed public-evidence/request-more hub and contextual links; only the approved illustrative QC asset is public, while facility, shipment/market, silicone, and regulatory evidence remain pending. Index and buyer-use monitoring are not yet mature.
affected_scope: Evidence hub and all high-intent pages
business_impact: A verifiable asset can improve buyer confidence, linkability, and qualification quality without promising ranking or indexing.
recommended_action: Use the implementation specification in the main report and release only Compliance-approved files and copy.
acceptance_test: Approved assets are crawlable, downloadable, tracked without PII, and linked in context; 30/60-day inspection and buyer-use metrics are recorded.
rollback: Remove assets and contextual links; retain the prior evidence request content.

observation: The 2026-08-10 URL Inspection baseline shows 27 of 30 URLs indexed; /applications/ was unknown to Google, while /resources/ and /quality/evidence/ were discovered but not indexed.
evidence: reports/gsc/gsc-inspect-all-2026-08-10T13-57-57-879Z.json; production releases e1613c9 and a5f3a1c now give all three hubs distinct buyer jobs and validated crawlable paths. Observe at 30 and 60 days without repeated index requests.
business_impact: The three intended navigation and evidence paths cannot currently earn Google search visibility as indexed landing pages.
recommended_action: Give each page a unique buyer job and stronger first-party value; use existing crawlable internal links and observe rather than repeatedly requesting indexing.
acceptance_test: At 30 and 60 days URL Inspection records a fetch/index status change or a documented decision to merge/retain; indexing itself is not guaranteed.
rollback: Remove only the new modules and links; do not redirect or delete without a separate approved migration plan.

observation: Differentiate Applications as a channel decision matrix, Resources as a guided procurement taxonomy, and Quality Evidence as a versioned proof library.
evidence: Production releases e1613c9 and a5f3a1c differentiate all three hubs: Applications is a five-model channel/RFQ matrix, Resources is a guided procurement taxonomy, and Quality Evidence is a mixed proof/request library. Canonical, schema-visible parity, internal links, HTTP, and mobile PageSpeed validation passed.
business_impact: Improves user value and reduces the risk that these hubs are treated as generic or low-value aggregates.
recommended_action: Add unique decisions, examples, limitations, and evidence; keep canonical, sitemap, and internal links stable.
acceptance_test: A reviewer can state a different job-to-be-done for each page; content is not duplicated; crawlable links and schema match visible content.
rollback: Restore the prior page sections from version control.

observation: Production baseline matched b86702b while the working tree also contained unrelated and previously unreviewed changes, creating mixed-release risk.
evidence: Commit e1613c9 contains exactly 29 approved SEO release files; applications, assets/main.js, pads-liners, zh/contact, the unrelated gpt-site deletion, and three older audit files remained unstaged. Vercel production was verified across all 30 URLs against the commit body.
business_impact: A broad deploy could mix approved SEO work with unrelated or unreviewed changes and make rollback ambiguous.
recommended_action: Extract approved audit actions into a clean, reviewable batch and explicitly exclude the unrelated deletion and any unsupported candidate copy.
dependencies: Owner review of existing dirty worktree
acceptance_test: The implementation diff contains only approved files, has a before/after evidence list, passes tests, and can be reverted as one batch.
rollback: Revert the dedicated batch only; preserve all pre-existing user work separately.

observation: Treat existing local SEO edits as candidates, not completed work; compare each against this audit, Compliance approval, live behavior, and a clean deployment plan.
evidence: Applications was reviewed and released as a5f3a1c; Pads/Liners was evidence-gated and released as 1363466. Remaining unstaged candidates are the linked Chinese form localization in assets/main.js and structured zh/contact form; the gpt-site deletion and three older audit files remain unrelated and excluded.
business_impact: Prevents the report from overstating progress and avoids deploying partial or inconsistent corrections.
recommended_action: Build a disposition table: approve, revise, defer, or reject for every dirty SEO file before implementation.
acceptance_test: Every local candidate has an owner decision and no unrelated path enters the implementation batch.
rollback: No production rollback; keep candidate changes untouched until an approved batch exists.

observation: GSC date dimension for the latest 28 days reports 140 impressions and 1 click; page dimension reports 220 impressions and 1 click versus 26 impressions and 0 clicks in the previous exact 28-day page window. The sample is still too small for causal CTR conclusions.
evidence: reports/gsc/gsc-query-date-2026-07-11-to-2026-08-07-2026-08-10T13-38-18-224Z-94719.json; current and previous page reports
business_impact: The site has emerging visibility and its first recorded click, but not a stable acquisition channel.
recommended_action: Preserve dimension-specific baselines and refresh only pages that pass the opportunity rubric; do not combine page and date totals.
acceptance_test: Monthly report labels dimension and window, separates brand/non-brand, and never treats average position as a fixed rank.
rollback: No site rollback; revert only individual content tests.

observation: Prioritize Home, Contact, Quality, RFQ Checklist, About, Cup page, Cup MOQ, and Disc MOQ for evidence/intent review; run snippet tests only after claims and measurement are trustworthy.
evidence: Production release e1613c9 completed the evidence and buyer-intent review across all eight priority pages and removed unsupported claims. No snippet experiment was launched because measurement ownership and source approvals remain unresolved; 28-day observation starts from the release date.
business_impact: Uses existing visibility instead of creating thin new pages and makes low-volume tests interpretable.
recommended_action: Change one snippet or first-screen hypothesis at a time, log baseline and guardrails, and review after at least 28 days with low-volume caution.
acceptance_test: Before/after version, window, impressions, clicks, CTR, Contact arrival, and RFQ quality are documented; unsupported claims are absent.
rollback: Restore the prior title, description, or section from version control.

observation: The production baseline had three true HTML orphans and two Best/HowTo pages with only one unique source.
evidence: The 2026-08-10 production release and follow-up provide every priority Best/HowTo resource at least two semantically relevant source pages; each resource has crawlable next-step links to products, Contact, and/or the Evidence hub. Commit-level graph validation passed.
business_impact: Sitemap-only discovery and weak contextual paths make the articles harder to find and less useful in buyer journeys.
recommended_action: Add a small number of contextual links from the closest product, comparison, and resource pages with user-task anchors.
acceptance_test: Every priority resource has at least two semantically relevant production source pages and reciprocal next-step links; links are crawlable a[href].
rollback: Remove the contextual links only.

observation: Use the source-to-target map in the report and keep navigation, breadcrumbs, and visible ItemList content synchronized.
evidence: Production e6a7a29 passed the 30-URL crawl and commit-level source-to-target graph: priority resources have contextual anchors and reciprocal next steps, retained schema matches visible content, and no broken internal destinations were found.
affected_scope: Resource, product, evidence, and RFQ paths
business_impact: Improves buyer navigation without treating link count as an objective.
recommended_action: Review each link for placement context, anchor clarity, and buyer value; reject sitewide exact-match additions.
acceptance_test: Automated crawl and manual review agree on destinations and no broken or misleading anchors are introduced.
rollback: Revert the link additions.

observation: The production baseline used invisible FAQPage markup on multiple pages and redundant HowTo markup despite limited rich-result eligibility.
evidence: Production release e1613c9 removed invisible FAQPage blocks from 12 pages, removed redundant HowTo markup from How-to-Choose, and synchronized retained FAQ answers with visible copy. The live 30-URL JSON-LD parse and FAQ parity audit passed.
affected_scope: FAQ and HowTo schema across the 30-URL sitemap
business_impact: Schema maintenance does not currently create a defensible rich-result opportunity and can distract from evidence and content accuracy.
recommended_action: Keep only accurate, visible, maintainable schema; do not promise rich results or add unsupported types.
acceptance_test: Rich Results/JSON validation passes, schema text matches visible content, and reports make no rich-result guarantee.
rollback: Restore the previous JSON-LD block if a validated type regresses.

observation: Review Product and Organization fields for public evidence, and consider removing redundant FAQ/HowTo markup where maintenance cost exceeds semantic value.
evidence: Product schema exists on three product pages; FAQPage appears on policy pages as well as commercial pages.
affected_scope: Product pages, policy pages, and resource templates
business_impact: Reduces stale or misleading markup risk while preserving useful entity and breadcrumb signals.
recommended_action: Inventory each schema type, owner, source field, and visible-content dependency before removal.
acceptance_test: No structured field contains an unapproved claim; remaining markup validates and matches the page.
rollback: Reinsert the previous validated JSON-LD.

observation: Five English/Chinese page pairs have reciprocal hreflang, but x-default exists only for Home; Chinese pages have no proven demand or conversion export, and production /zh/contact/ is mailto-only while the structured form exists only as a local candidate.

affected_scope: Five Chinese URLs and their English pairs
business_impact: International expansion cannot be justified or measured, and Chinese claims can drift from English Compliance wording.

dependencies: Chinese lead records; YSEO-001; claim register
acceptance_test: A decision to maintain, strengthen, or stop expansion is recorded; paired pages pass reciprocal hreflang and claim parity checks.
rollback: Keep existing indexed pages and mailto route; do not expand until evidence is available.

observation: If Chinese is maintained, add consistent x-default policy where appropriate, deploy a reviewed structured RFQ path, and track Chinese inquiries separately from English traffic.
evidence: Google localized versions guidance requires reciprocal fully qualified alternates; current local form is not production.
affected_scope: Home, Products, OEM/ODM, Quality, Contact pairs
business_impact: Improves language routing and measurement without creating machine-translated thin pages.
recommended_action: Perform mother-tongue QA, privacy review, response testing, and hreflang validation as one controlled batch.
acceptance_test: All pairs list themselves and each other; the form passes controlled delivery tests; no unsupported translated claims remain.
rollback: Restore mailto-only contact and prior hreflang tags.

observation: Post-release mobile PageSpeed tests on Home, Cup, Quality, and Contact score 98-100 performance and 100 in SEO/accessibility/best practices; LCP is 1.2-2.1s and CLS 0, but no CrUX field LCP/INP/CLS is available.
evidence: reports/pagespeed/pagespeed-2026-08-10T15-19-41-790Z.json; reports/pagespeed/pagespeed-2026-08-10T15-20-03-653Z.json; reports/pagespeed/pagespeed-2026-08-10T15-20-19-120Z.json; reports/pagespeed/pagespeed-2026-08-10T15-20-39-061Z.json
affected_scope: Four critical templates; prior full-site lab report
business_impact: Performance is not the present P0/P1 bottleneck, but real user responsiveness cannot be claimed.
recommended_action: Preserve performance budgets and wait for field data or approved RUM before prioritizing optimization work.
acceptance_test: A 28-day field report exists or the site explicitly reports field data unavailable; lab regressions are blocked in review.
rollback: Remove only new monitoring code if it affects privacy or performance.

observation: The production baseline sitemap was valid with 30 canonical URLs but used a uniform lastmod, while GSC's indexed=0 sitemap aggregate conflicted with URL Inspection and search impressions.
evidence: Production e6a7a29 serves a valid 30-URL canonical sitemap; only 24 materially changed pages use 2026-08-10 lastmod and unchanged pages retain prior dates. Live body and canonical validation passed; sitemap submission is not treated as proof of indexing.
business_impact: The indexed=0 field is an unreliable aggregate here, and uniform lastmod weakens freshness precision.
recommended_action: Use URL Inspection and performance data for indexing truth; update lastmod only after significant page changes.
acceptance_test: Sitemap stays valid and canonical; changed pages have honest lastmod; no report treats sitemap submission as indexing success.
rollback: Regenerate the previous valid sitemap.

observation: No GSC Links export, backlink index, referral analytics, or newly verified independent editorial mention was available; 13 screened prospects exist, with Qmed and Suplivia evidence-blocked and Femtech Insider/INDA research-ready.
evidence: docs/seo/backlink-prospects.csv; validated scorer output; docs/seo/authority-growth-weekly-2026-07-27.md
business_impact: The site cannot quantify link equity, referral quality, unlinked mentions, or competitor authority gaps.
recommended_action: Acquire a GSC Links export or approved backlink source and publish evidence before manual editorial distribution.
acceptance_test: A verified source list distinguishes editorial, controlled, irrelevant, lost, and risky links; referral and RFQ outcomes are measured.
rollback: No site rollback; stop any outreach and remove only inaccurate submitted materials.

observation: After evidence approval, manually pursue a small number of relevant directories or editorial opportunities; prohibit paid links, exchanges, mass guest posts, and unsupported certificate claims.
evidence: Prospect scorer: Femtech Insider 19 research-ready, INDA 17 research-ready; official Google/Bing spam guidance
business_impact: Builds discoverability as a by-product of verifiable value and reduces link-spam risk.
recommended_action: Require user approval for every external submission and use UTM-tagged destination pages without sensitive data.
acceptance_test: Each live mention is independently verifiable and any referral visit/RFQ is attributed; link count and DR are not success KPIs.
rollback: Request correction or removal from the publisher; stop the campaign.

observation: A nonexistent URL returns a correct HTTP 404 but only Vercel plain text, with no branded navigation or recovery path.
evidence: HEAD request to /definitely-not-a-real-page-20260810/ returned HTTP 404 and x-vercel-error=NOT_FOUND
business_impact: Users and crawlers receive the correct status, but buyers have no path back to products, resources, or contact.
recommended_action: Add a lightweight branded 404 that preserves the 404 status and offers Home, Products, Resources, and Contact links.
acceptance_test: Unknown URLs still return 404, not 200; page loads without JS and exposes four crawlable recovery links.
rollback: Remove the custom 404 and return to Vercel default.

observation: robots allows crawling, but no Bing Webmaster, IndexNow, AI referral, Copilot, or AI-answer citation dataset was available.
evidence: robots.txt; repository report inventory; Bing Webmaster official guidance
affected_scope: Non-Google discovery and AI referral reporting
business_impact: No evidence supports investing in new engines or claiming AI visibility.
recommended_action: Measure demand first; keep classic search, Bing, AI referrals, and conversions separate.
acceptance_test: A quarterly engine/referral report exists or explicitly records zero/unknown data; no AI schema or visibility guarantee is used.
rollback: Stop the experiment and remove optional submission integration.

observation: Do not create another indexable page until the new-page gate is met: distinct intent, B2B decision value, YUJI evidence, internal path, conversion destination, and more than one isolated impression or independent buyer evidence.
evidence: Only seven query rows are visible in 90 days; protective-cover demand is two impressions; existing pages already cover cup, disc, pads, MOQ, supplier choice, and RFQ tasks.
business_impact: Prevents cannibalization, scaled low-value content, and maintenance burden.
recommended_action: Use the page-action plan and sales feedback to decide UPDATE versus CREATE; default to refreshing an existing relevant URL.
acceptance_test: Every proposed URL has a signed brief satisfying all six gates and a 30/60/90 review plan.
rollback: Do not publish or noindex/remove the test page under a separately approved plan if it fails.
